instructions: Follow docs/content-wave-1/prompts/dedupe.md. Review every planned stub of every topic in the item against each other and against the existing inventory. Answer with the findings; an empty list when nothing needs fixing.

items.text:
Planned stubs (stubId | topic | level | type | angle | answerHinge):
- csharp-01 | csharp | junior | output | What does a snippet print that reads `s?.Length ?? -1` for a null string and for a non-null string? | `?.` short-circuits to null when the receiver is null, and `??` then supplies the right operand, so the null string yields -1 instead of throwing.
- csharp-02 | csharp | junior | output | What does a snippet print that compares two separately created positional records with equal values using `==` and `ReferenceEquals`? | A record class (C# 9) gets compiler-generated value-based equality, so `==` is True while `ReferenceEquals` is False for two distinct instances.
- csharp-03 | csharp | junior | output | What does a snippet print after creating a modified copy of a record with a `with` expression and printing both the original and the copy? | A `with` expression creates a new record with the listed properties changed and leaves the original instance untouched.
- csharp-04 | csharp | junior | output | What does a switch expression with relational arms `< 0`, `< 20` and a discard print for the input 15? | Switch expression arms are tested top to bottom and the first matching arm wins, so 15 matches `< 20` (relational patterns, C# 9).
- csharp-05 | csharp | junior | output | What does a snippet print when three methods are combined into one `Action` with `+=`, one is removed with `-=`, and the delegate is invoked? | A multicast delegate invokes its invocation list in the order the delegates were added, and `-=` removes the matching method from that list.
- csharp-06 | csharp | junior | single | What changes for a `string` variable when `<Nullable>enable</Nullable>` is turned on in a project? | Nullable reference types (C# 8) only add compile-time annotations and warnings; the compiled code and runtime behaviour of `string` do not change and no runtime null checks are inserted.
- csharp-07 | csharp | junior | open | Why does a generic `Max<T>` method fail to compile when it calls `CompareTo` on `T`, and how does a `where` clause fix it? | Without a constraint the compiler only knows `T` as `object`, so a constraint such as `where T : IComparable<T>` is what makes the interface members callable and restricts which type arguments are allowed.
- csharp-08 | csharp | junior | multi | Which members does the compiler generate for a positional `record class Person(string Name, int Age)`? | A positional record class gets value-based Equals/GetHashCode/==, a ToString listing the properties, a Deconstruct method and init-only properties, but no public setters and no IComparable implementation.
- csharp-09 | csharp | junior | find-bug | In a `#nullable enable` snippet that silences a warning with `name!.Length` on a value from a lookup that returns null, find the line that crashes. | The `!` operator only suppresses the compiler warning and does nothing at runtime, so dereferencing the null value still throws NullReferenceException.
- csharp-10 | csharp | middle | output | What does a snippet print that tests a null `object` with `o is var x` and with `o is object`? | The `var` pattern always matches, including null, while a type pattern such as `is object` never matches null, so the results are True and False.
- csharp-11 | csharp | middle | output | What does `==` print for two records whose `int[]` property holds different array instances with the same elements? | Record equality compares each member with EqualityComparer<T>.Default, which for arrays is reference equality, so the records are not equal despite identical contents.
- csharp-12 | csharp | middle | output | What does a snippet print when it invokes a `Func<int>` that combines three lambdas returning 1, 2 and 3? | All delegates in the invocation list run, but the call returns only the value of the last delegate invoked, so the other return values are discarded.
- csharp-13 | csharp | middle | find-bug | In a snippet that subscribes a lambda to an event, later writes `-=` with an identical lambda and raises the event, find the line that fails to unsubscribe the handler. | Each lambda expression creates a new delegate instance, so `-=` with a textually identical lambda finds no match and the original handler keeps running; the delegate must be stored in a variable to be removed.
- csharp-14 | csharp | middle | single | Which of several assignments of a `List<string>` to variables of `List<object>`, `IList<object>`, `IEnumerable<object>` and `ICollection<object>` compiles? | Only `IEnumerable<out T>` is covariant; classes such as `List<T>` and read-write interfaces such as `IList<T>` and `ICollection<T>` are invariant.
- csharp-15 | csharp | middle | open | What does declaring a member with the `event` keyword protect against compared with exposing a public delegate field of the same type? | Outside the declaring type an event allows only `+=` and `-=`, so other code cannot invoke it or overwrite the whole invocation list with `=`, which a public delegate field allows.
- csharp-16 | csharp | middle | multi | A project is pinned to `<LangVersion>11</LangVersion>`; which of these features fail to compile until it moves to C# 12? | Primary constructors on non-record classes and collection expressions arrived in C# 12, while records (C# 9), file-scoped namespaces (C# 10) and raw string literals (C# 11) already work in C# 11.
- csharp-17 | csharp | senior | output | What does `==` print when a base record `A(1)` is compared with a derived record `B(1) : A(1)` that adds no members? | Record equality also compares the compiler-generated EqualityContract (the runtime type), so instances of different record types are never equal even with identical values.
- csharp-18 | csharp | senior | output | What happens when a lambda marked `static` reads a local variable of the enclosing method? | A `static` lambda (C# 9) is forbidden from capturing locals, parameters or `this`, so the code fails to compile instead of allocating a closure.
- csharp-19 | csharp | senior | output | What does a snippet print after incrementing `Counter<int>.Count` twice and `Counter<string>.Count` once and printing both? | Each closed constructed generic type has its own copy of static fields, so `Counter<int>` and `Counter<string>` keep separate counters (2 and 1).
- csharp-20 | csharp | senior | find-bug | A method meant to treat a character as a consonant when it is neither 'a' nor 'e' uses `c is not 'a' or 'e'` and misclassifies 'e'; find the defective line. | `not` binds tighter than `or`, so the pattern means `(not 'a') or 'e'`, which matches 'e'; the intended check is `is not ('a' or 'e')` or `is not 'a' and not 'e'`.
- csharp-21 | csharp | senior | open | How does the C# compiler implement a lambda that captures a local variable, and what consequences does that have for the variable's lifetime and for allocations? | Captured locals are hoisted into fields of a compiler-generated closure class shared by all lambdas in that scope, so the variable lives as long as any delegate referencing it and each scope entry allocates a closure object.
- csharp-22 | csharp | senior | open | Why does a custom `bool TryFind(string key, out string? value)` method produce false warnings at call sites, and how do nullable analysis attributes fix it? | Flow analysis does not look inside the method body, so the signature must state the contract with attributes such as `[NotNullWhen(true)]` to tell callers that `value` is non-null when the method returns true.
- csharp-23 | csharp | lead | single | Which rollout plan for enabling nullable reference types in a large legacy solution with many teams carries the least risk? | Enabling the feature incrementally (per project or file, starting from leaf projects and with warnings as errors only once a project is clean) keeps builds green and avoids mass `!` suppressions that hide real nulls.
- types-memory-01 | types-memory | junior | output | A snippet assigns one struct variable to another, changes a field through the second variable and prints the field from both. | Assigning a struct copies all of its fields, so changing the copy leaves the original unchanged.
- types-memory-02 | types-memory | junior | output | A method receives a List<int> without ref, adds an item, then assigns a new list to the parameter, and the caller prints the count. | A reference is passed by value, so the caller sees a change made through the reference but not a reassignment of the parameter.
- types-memory-03 | types-memory | junior | single | Which of several statements that use an int variable performs boxing: assignment to object, widening to long, calling ToString, or List<int>.Add? | Boxing happens only when a value type is converted to object or an interface type; a numeric conversion, an overridden ToString call and a generic List<int> do not box.
- types-memory-04 | types-memory | junior | open | Is it true that value types live on the stack and reference types live on the heap, and where does an int field of a class instance actually live? | Where a value is stored depends on where the variable lives, not on its type: a value type field of a class, an array element or a captured local is stored on the heap inside the containing object.
- types-memory-05 | types-memory | junior | multi | Select every value type among int, an enum, int[], string, a record struct and int?. | Enums, record structs and Nullable<T> are value types, while arrays are reference types even when their elements are value types.
- types-memory-06 | types-memory | middle | output | A snippet boxes an int into an object variable, then changes the int and prints both the object and the int. | Boxing copies the value into a new heap object, so later changes to the original variable do not affect the boxed copy.
- types-memory-07 | types-memory | middle | find-bug | A class holds a mutable struct counter in a readonly field and calls its Increment method, but the printed count stays 0; find the defective line. | Calling a mutating method on a readonly field of a non-readonly struct operates on a defensive copy, so the field itself never changes.
- types-memory-08 | types-memory | middle | output | A snippet compares two struct instances with equal fields and two class instances with equal fields using Equals and prints both results. | ValueType.Equals compares the field values of structs, while object.Equals on a class without an override compares references.
- types-memory-09 | types-memory | middle | single | Which of several candidate types is the best fit for a struct according to the .NET framework design guidelines? | A struct fits a small (under about 16 bytes), immutable type that logically represents a single value and is rarely boxed; large, mutable or identity-bearing types should be classes.
- types-memory-10 | types-memory | middle | output | A snippet takes a Span<int> slice of an array, writes to the slice and prints the array. | Slicing a Span<T> creates a view over the same memory without copying, so writes through the slice change the underlying array.
- types-memory-11 | types-memory | middle | multi | In C# 13 on .NET 9 or later, where may a Span<int> be used: a local in a synchronous method, a method parameter, a field of a ref struct, a field of a class, a List<Span<int>> element, a variable captured by a lambda? | Span<T> is a ref struct that must never escape to the heap, so it is allowed as a local, a parameter and a ref struct field, but not as a class field, a generic argument of List<T> or a captured variable.
- types-memory-12 | types-memory | middle | output | A snippet takes a ref local to a[0], assigns a new array to a, writes through the ref local and prints a[0] of the new array and of the saved old array. | A ref local aliases the storage location of the element in the original array object, not the variable a, so the write lands in the old array.
- types-memory-13 | types-memory | senior | output | A mutable struct implements ICounter; the snippet assigns it to an ICounter variable, calls Inc twice through the interface and once on the struct, then prints both counts. | Converting a struct to an interface boxes a copy, so interface calls mutate the box and direct calls mutate the original independently.
- types-memory-14 | types-memory | senior | output | A snippet boxes a null int? and an int? holding 5 into object variables and prints whether the first is null and the type name of the second. | Boxing a Nullable<T> without a value yields a null reference, and boxing one with a value yields a boxed T, never a boxed Nullable<T>.
- types-memory-15 | types-memory | senior | open | A 64-byte mutable struct is passed through several method layers in a hot loop; when does this cost more than a class, and what can reduce the cost? | Every pass and assignment copies the whole struct, so for large structs copying can outweigh the saved allocation; making it a readonly struct and passing it by in or ref removes copies and defensive copies.
- types-memory-16 | types-memory | senior | single | A parser must keep a reference to a slice of an input buffer in a class field and use it after an await; which type should hold the slice? | Memory<T> is not a ref struct and can live on the heap and across await, while Span<T> cannot, so the field should be Memory<T> and code converts it to Span<T> only for synchronous processing.
- types-memory-17 | types-memory | senior | find-bug | Code calls Monitor.Enter and Monitor.Exit with an int field as the lock object and throws SynchronizationLockException; find the defective line. | Each call boxes the int into a new object, so Monitor.Exit receives a different object than the one locked by Monitor.Enter.
- types-memory-18 | types-memory | lead | open | A developer proposes converting many domain and DTO classes to structs to reduce allocations across the codebase; how do you decide and what rules do you set for the team? | Converting to structs changes semantics (copying, default values, equality, boxing) and can break public APIs, so allow it only for small immutable value-like types on measured hot paths, with benchmarks and review guidance rather than a blanket change.
- oop-solid-01 | oop-solid | junior | output | What does the program print when one derived method uses override and another uses new, and both are called through a base-class variable? | A call through a base-typed reference dispatches to the override, but a method declared with new only hides the base method, so the base version runs.
- oop-solid-02 | oop-solid | junior | output | What does the program print when a class has a public Print method and also an explicit IPrinter.Print implementation, called once through the class and once through the interface? | An explicit interface implementation is reachable only through an interface-typed reference, so the class-typed call runs the public method and the interface-typed call runs the explicit one.
- oop-solid-03 | oop-solid | junior | find-bug | An Order class validates items in AddItem and keeps a running total, but its Items property returns the private List<T>; find the line that lets caller code break the total. | Returning the internal mutable list lets callers add items without going through AddItem, so the invariant between items and total breaks; expose a read-only view instead.
- oop-solid-04 | oop-solid | junior | open | What does the single responsibility principle mean, and how would you tell that a ReportService that loads data, formats HTML and sends email violates it? | A class should have one reason to change; data access, formatting and delivery change for different reasons and stakeholders, so they belong in separate classes.
- oop-solid-05 | oop-solid | junior | single | Which statement correctly describes the interface segregation principle? | Clients should not be forced to depend on members they do not use, so large interfaces are split into smaller, client-specific ones.
- oop-solid-06 | oop-solid | junior | single | For three fixed discount rules that rarely change, which implementation does the KISS principle favour: plain conditionals, a reflection-based plugin loader, a configurable rules engine, or a DSL? | KISS favours the simplest design that meets the actual requirement, so plain conditionals win while the rules are few and fixed.
- oop-solid-07 | oop-solid | junior | multi | Given a list of decisions in a pull request, select all that violate YAGNI. | YAGNI is violated by building capability for a speculative future need (an unused second storage provider, a config switch nobody asked for), not by extracting shared code or testing current requirements.
- oop-solid-08 | oop-solid | middle | output | What happens when code calls a default interface method (C# 8 and later) through a variable typed as the implementing class that does not declare that method? | A default interface member is not inherited by the class, so it is accessible only through the interface type and the class-typed call is a compile error CS1061.
- oop-solid-09 | oop-solid | middle | output | What does the program print when a base constructor calls a virtual method whose override reads a field that the derived constructor body assigns? | The base constructor runs before the derived constructor body, so the override executes on a partially constructed object and sees the field's default value.
- oop-solid-10 | oop-solid | middle | output | What area does a method print after setting Width to 5 and Height to 4 on a Rectangle variable that holds a Square whose setters keep both sides equal? | The Square override makes the last setter win and prints 16 instead of the expected 20, showing that the subtype breaks the base contract and violates LSP.
- oop-solid-11 | oop-solid | middle | find-bug | A CountingBag derives from a Bag whose virtual AddRange calls the virtual Add, and overrides both to count additions; find the line that makes the count double. | The subclass depends on an undocumented self-call in the base class, so overriding AddRange to count again double-counts; wrapping the bag by composition avoids relying on base internals.
- oop-solid-12 | oop-solid | middle | open | When would you choose composition over inheritance to reuse behaviour, and when is inheritance still the right tool? | Inheritance fits a true is-a relationship with a stable base contract designed for extension; composition is preferred for reusing behaviour because it hides implementation, allows swapping at runtime and avoids coupling to base-class internals.
- oop-solid-13 | oop-solid | middle | single | OrderService creates a SqlOrderRepository with new; which change applies the dependency inversion principle? | DIP means the high-level module defines an abstraction it needs (IOrderRepository) and receives an implementation, so the low-level SQL class depends on that abstraction rather than the reverse.
- oop-solid-14 | oop-solid | senior | output | What does the program print when Base implements IGreeter with a non-virtual method and Derived re-lists IGreeter and hides Greet with new, called through IGreeter and through Base? | Re-declaring the interface in Derived re-maps IGreeter.Greet to Derived's member, so the interface call prints the derived text while the Base-typed call still runs the base method.
- oop-solid-15 | oop-solid | senior | open | Two teams' invoice and payroll modules share a helper that was extracted because the code looked identical, and now every change needs flags and branches; what went wrong and how do you fix it? | DRY is about duplicated knowledge, not duplicated text; code that changes for different reasons was merged into a wrong abstraction, and the fix is to inline it back and re-extract only what truly shares one reason to change.
- oop-solid-16 | oop-solid | senior | situation | Every sprint someone edits a large switch on payment provider type spread across five classes, and each edit causes regressions in other providers; what do you do? | Apply the open/closed principle where variation actually recurs: move provider-specific behaviour behind one abstraction with an implementation per provider registered in one place, so adding a provider means adding code rather than editing shared branches.
- collections-linq-01 | collections-linq | junior | output | A Where query is defined over a List<int>, an item is added to the list afterwards, and then Count() of the query is printed. | The query stores only the source and the predicate, so it runs when Count() enumerates it and sees the item added after the query was defined.
- collections-linq-02 | collections-linq | junior | output | The snippet adds the same string to a HashSet<string> twice and prints both Add results and the Count. | HashSet<T>.Add returns false and leaves the set unchanged when an equal element already exists, so the output is True False 1.
- collections-linq-03 | collections-linq | junior | output | The snippet reads a key that was never added through the Dictionary<string, int> indexer, and the question asks what happens. | The Dictionary indexer getter throws KeyNotFoundException for a missing key instead of returning a default value. TryGetValue is the non-throwing alternative.
- collections-linq-04 | collections-linq | junior | output | The snippet calls First() on a Where query that matches no elements, and the question asks what happens. | First throws InvalidOperationException when the sequence is empty. Only FirstOrDefault returns the default value.
- collections-linq-05 | collections-linq | junior | single | What is the time complexity of List<T>.Insert(0, item) on a list of n elements? | List<T> is backed by an array, so inserting at index 0 shifts every existing element and costs O(n).
- collections-linq-06 | collections-linq | junior | single | Which BCL collection fits an undo history in which the most recent action is always undone first? | Undo is last-in-first-out, which is exactly Stack<T>, with O(1) Push and Pop. Queue<T> is first-in-first-out.
- collections-linq-07 | collections-linq | junior | open | What does each of IEnumerable<T>, ICollection<T> and IList<T> add, and which should a method parameter accept? | IEnumerable<T> only allows forward iteration. ICollection<T> adds Count, Add, Remove and Contains. IList<T> adds index access. A parameter should ask for the least capable interface the method needs.
- collections-linq-08 | collections-linq | junior | multi | Select every collection whose lookup of an element or key is O(1) on average: Dictionary<TKey,TValue>, HashSet<T>, List<T>, SortedDictionary<TKey,TValue>, LinkedList<T>. | Only the hash-based Dictionary and HashSet give O(1) average lookup. SortedDictionary is a tree with O(log n) lookup, and List and LinkedList search linearly in O(n).
- collections-linq-09 | collections-linq | middle | output | An object whose GetHashCode uses a mutable Id is added to a HashSet, its Id is then changed, and the snippet prints Contains for the same object and the Count of the set. | The set stored the old hash code, so a lookup with the new hash code fails even for the same reference. Contains prints False while Count stays 1.
- collections-linq-10 | collections-linq | middle | output | People are sorted with OrderBy(p => p.Age).OrderBy(p => p.Name) and printed, and the question asks for the resulting order. | The second OrderBy becomes the primary sort and replaces the first. Because OrderBy is a stable sort, age only breaks ties between equal names, which is the reverse of OrderBy(Age).ThenBy(Name).
- collections-linq-11 | collections-linq | middle | output | A Dictionary<string,int> is created with StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase, then values are assigned to "Key" and "KEY", and the snippet prints Count and the stored value. | The comparer supplies both hashing and equality, so the two keys are the same key and the second assignment overwrites the first. The output is 1 and the second value.
- collections-linq-12 | collections-linq | middle | find-bug | A class overrides Equals but not GetHashCode and is used as a Dictionary key. ContainsKey with an equal new instance prints False instead of True; find the defective line. | Hash-based collections compare hash codes before calling Equals. The inherited reference-based GetHashCode gives equal objects different hashes, which breaks the rule that equal objects must have equal hash codes.
- collections-linq-13 | collections-linq | middle | single | A helper takes a Func<Order, bool> parameter and calls db.Orders.Where(predicate). Where is the filter executed? | A Func cannot bind to Queryable.Where, which needs an Expression<Func<...>>, so overload resolution picks Enumerable.Where. All rows are loaded and then filtered in memory.
- collections-linq-14 | collections-linq | middle | multi | Select the true statements about SortedDictionary<TKey,TValue> and SortedList<TKey,TValue>: insertion cost, memory use, key order and index access. | Both keep keys sorted. SortedList is a pair of arrays: it uses less memory and allows index access, but inserting unsorted data costs O(n). SortedDictionary is a tree with O(log n) insertion and removal.
- collections-linq-15 | collections-linq | middle | open | Why is List<T>.Add called amortized O(1), what happens when Count reaches Capacity, and when should you set the capacity up front? | When the list is full it allocates an array of double the capacity and copies the elements. That single Add is O(n), but doubling keeps the average cost O(1). Presetting the capacity avoids repeated copies when the final size is known.
- collections-linq-16 | collections-linq | senior | output | A custom yield-based extension method checks its argument for null and throws. The snippet calls it with null, prints a marker, then enumerates the result inside try/catch and prints the caught exception type. | The whole body of an iterator method, including argument checks, runs only on the first MoveNext. The marker prints first and the ArgumentNullException appears only during enumeration.
- collections-linq-17 | collections-linq | senior | output | A SortedSet<string> uses a comparer that compares only string length. The snippet adds "aa", "bb" and "c" and prints Count. | Sorted collections treat a comparer result of 0 as equality, so "bb" counts as a duplicate of "aa" and is not added. Count is 2.
- collections-linq-18 | collections-linq | senior | find-bug | Items are created with ids.Select(id => new Item(id)), each is marked Done in a foreach loop, and Count(i => i.Done) then prints 0 instead of 3; find the line to fix. | The Select query is not materialised, so every enumeration runs the projection again and builds new Item objects. The mutations were made on objects that no longer exist; ToList() fixes it.
- collections-linq-19 | collections-linq | senior | open | How does Dictionary<TKey,TValue> find a key internally, and what happens to its performance when the key type's GetHashCode returns the same value for many keys? | The hash code selects a bucket, and equal-bucket entries are chained and compared one by one with Equals. A poorly distributed GetHashCode puts all keys in one chain, so lookup and insert degrade from O(1) to O(n).
- collections-linq-20 | collections-linq | lead | situation | After two incidents where whole tables were loaded into memory, the team argues whether repositories should return IQueryable<T> or IEnumerable<T>. How do you settle it and prevent a repeat? | Make an explicit, documented choice. Either keep IQueryable inside the data layer and expose purpose-built query methods that return materialised results, or allow IQueryable deliberately and accept that the persistence boundary leaks. Back the choice with review rules, query logging and tests that check the generated SQL.
- clr-gc-01 | clr-gc | junior | single | Asks what happens to an IDisposable object that is never disposed when it becomes unreachable and the garbage collector reclaims it. | The garbage collector never calls Dispose. It only reclaims memory, plus running a finalizer if the type has one, so unmanaged resources wait until finalization or leak.
- clr-gc-02 | clr-gc | junior | single | Asks which set of parts a compiled .NET assembly contains. | An assembly holds IL code, type metadata and a manifest that describes its identity, version and references. It does not hold native machine code for the JIT path.
- clr-gc-03 | clr-gc | junior | output | Shows two using declarations in one method whose Dispose methods print their names, and asks what the program prints. | Resources from using declarations are disposed at the end of the enclosing scope in reverse order of declaration, so the second resource is disposed first.
- clr-gc-04 | clr-gc | junior | open | Asks what the JIT compiler does and when a method's IL becomes native code. | The runtime compiles a method's IL to native code the first time the method is called. The result is reused for later calls in the same process, so the first call pays the compilation cost.
- clr-gc-05 | clr-gc | middle | output | Prints GC.GetGeneration of a still-referenced object after allocation and after each of two GC.Collect calls, and asks for the output. | A new small object starts in generation 0, and each collection it survives promotes it one generation up to generation 2, so the output is 0 1 2.
- clr-gc-06 | clr-gc | middle | output | Prints GC.GetGeneration for a fresh byte[84000] and a fresh byte[85000], and asks for the output. | Objects of 85,000 bytes or more go to the large object heap, which is collected with generation 2, so GC.GetGeneration reports 2 right after allocation. The smaller array starts in generation 0.
- clr-gc-07 | clr-gc | middle | output | Prints typeof(string).Assembly.GetName().Name on .NET 10 and asks for the output, with mscorlib and System.Runtime among the options. | In .NET (Core) the core types are implemented in System.Private.CoreLib. System.Runtime is only a reference facade and mscorlib belongs to .NET Framework, so the output is System.Private.CoreLib.
- clr-gc-08 | clr-gc | middle | find-bug | A StreamWriter writes text into a MemoryStream without being disposed or flushed, then the code prints the stream length and gets 0, and the reader must find the defective line. | StreamWriter buffers its output and writes it to the underlying stream only on Flush or Dispose, so leaving out the using block leaves the data in the buffer.
- clr-gc-09 | clr-gc | middle | find-bug | A short-lived subscriber attaches a handler to a static event and is never detached, and a WeakReference check after GC.Collect prints True instead of False. | The static event's delegate holds a strong reference to the subscriber, so the subscriber stays reachable from a static root until the handler is removed.
- clr-gc-10 | clr-gc | middle | single | Asks why a service that keeps allocating and freeing large arrays of different sizes can show LOH fragmentation, and which setting changes that. | By default the GC sweeps the large object heap but does not compact it. Compaction happens only on request, for example with GCSettings.LargeObjectHeapCompactionMode set to CompactOnce before a full blocking collection.
- clr-gc-11 | clr-gc | middle | multi | Asks the reader to select every kind of reference that the garbage collector treats as a root. | Static fields, live local variables and parameters of executing methods, and strong GC handles are roots. A WeakReference target and an object referenced only by another unreachable object are not.
- clr-gc-12 | clr-gc | senior | output | A program creates an object whose finalizer prints a line, drops the reference and ends with a final print and no GC calls, and the question asks what .NET 10 prints. | Unlike .NET Framework, .NET (Core) does not run finalizers when the process exits, so only the final line is printed.
- clr-gc-13 | clr-gc | senior | find-bug | A derived class overrides protected virtual Dispose(bool) to release its own resource but never calls the base implementation, so the program prints that the base resource is still open. | In the dispose pattern each override of Dispose(bool) must call base.Dispose(disposing), otherwise the resources owned by the base class are never released.
- clr-gc-14 | clr-gc | senior | single | Asks why an unreachable object with a finalizer is not reclaimed in the collection that finds it unreachable, and what this costs. | The GC moves an unreachable finalizable object to the f-reachable queue, which is a root, so the object and everything it references survive and are promoted. The memory is freed only by a later collection after the finalizer thread has run the finalizer.
- clr-gc-15 | clr-gc | senior | open | Asks how workstation and server GC differ and when you would choose each for a service running in a memory-limited container. | Server GC uses one heap and one GC thread per core for throughput, at the cost of larger memory use. - aspnet-core-18 | aspnet-core | senior | open | What happens to hosted services and in-flight work when the host receives SIGTERM, and what limits how long they get to finish? | The host signals stopping and calls StopAsync on hosted services in reverse order, cancelling the stopping token, and waits at most HostOptions.ShutdownTimeout (30 seconds by default since .NET 6) before ending the process.
- aspnet-core-19 | aspnet-core | senior | situation | After moving the app behind a TLS-terminating load balancer, generated links use http and logs show the balancer address as every client IP; what do you do? | Kestrel only sees the proxy connection, so the app must use the Forwarded Headers middleware early in the pipeline with KnownProxies or KnownNetworks configured to trust X-Forwarded-Proto and X-Forwarded-For.
- aspnet-core-20 | aspnet-core | senior | situation | On .NET 8 an app never logs that it is listening after a BackgroundService was added whose ExecuteAsync starts with a synchronous polling loop; how do you diagnose and fix it? | Before .NET 10, BackgroundService.StartAsync runs ExecuteAsync synchronously until its first await, so synchronous work blocks host startup; yield early, move the loop to async code, or rely on .NET 10 where ExecuteAsync runs entirely as a background task.
- aspnet-core-21 | aspnet-core | lead | situation | Half of your team wants new endpoints in minimal APIs while an existing service has 150 controller actions with MVC filters; how do you decide and roll out the choice? | The decision rests on which controller features the service depends on (MVC filters, conventions, model binding behaviour) and on consistency cost: mixing both in one service is supported but cross-cutting logic must be duplicated as endpoint filters, so set an explicit rule per service and migrate only with a reason.
- aspnet-core-22 | aspnet-core | architect | open | How would you design configuration management for 40 ASP.NET Core services so that settings can change at runtime without redeploys, and what risks does it bring? | Add a central store as another IConfiguration provider with local values as fallback, have code read IOptionsMonitor for reloadable settings, and treat runtime changes as deployments: versioned, validated, audited and rolled out gradually because a bad value now reaches every service at once.
- web-api-01 | web-api | junior | open | Asks what makes an HTTP API RESTful: resources identified by URLs, a uniform interface of standard methods, representations and stateless requests. | REST models nouns as resources addressed by URLs and manipulated through the standard HTTP methods, with each request carrying all the state the server needs.
- web-api-02 | web-api | junior | open | Asks how PUT and PATCH differ when updating a resource and what happens to fields the client omits. | PUT replaces the whole target representation with the one sent, while PATCH applies a set of partial changes described by the request body.
- web-api-03 | web-api | junior | single | Asks which response a POST that creates a new resource should return. | 201 Created with a Location header pointing at the new resource is the response RFC 9110 defines for successful creation.
- web-api-04 | web-api | junior | multi | Asks the reader to select all HTTP methods that RFC 9110 defines as idempotent from a list including POST and PATCH. | GET, HEAD, PUT, DELETE and OPTIONS are idempotent by definition, while POST and PATCH are not.
- web-api-05 | web-api | junior | single | Asks how a WebSocket connection is established and which status code the server returns on success. | The client sends an HTTP/1.1 GET with Upgrade: websocket and the server answers 101 Switching Protocols, after which the TCP connection carries WebSocket frames.
- web-api-06 | web-api | middle | find-bug | A runnable snippet uses HttpClient with a stub HttpMessageHandler that prints the request URI; BaseAddress lacks a trailing slash, so the version segment is lost and the wrong URL is printed. | Relative URIs are resolved by RFC 3986 rules, so a BaseAddress without a trailing slash has its last segment replaced and a relative path with a leading slash replaces the whole path.
- web-api-07 | web-api | middle | open | Asks to compare versioning a web API through the URL path, a query string parameter and a header or media type, and when to pick each. | URL path versions are explicit and cache-friendly but change resource identity, while header or media type versions keep URLs stable at the cost of discoverability and tooling support.
- web-api-08 | web-api | middle | single | Asks why a browser application cannot call a standard gRPC service directly and what ASP.NET Core offers instead. | Browser APIs do not give the low-level control over HTTP/2 frames and trailers that gRPC needs, so browsers need gRPC-Web or a JSON transcoding endpoint.
- web-api-09 | web-api | middle | open | Asks how to make a POST that creates a payment safe for client retries after a timeout. | The client sends a unique Idempotency-Key and the server stores the key with the outcome, returning the stored result for a repeated key instead of executing the operation again.
- web-api-10 | web-api | middle | multi | Asks the reader to select the error status codes with which the HTTP RFCs define the Retry-After header to tell the client when to try again, from a list including 400, 404, 409, 429 and 503. | Retry-After is defined for 503 Service Unavailable in RFC 9110 and for 429 Too Many Requests in RFC 6585, not for client errors such as 400, 404 or 409.
- web-api-11 | web-api | middle | single | Asks how to keep a long-lived static HttpClient from ignoring DNS changes without falling back to creating a client per request. | Setting SocketsHttpHandler.PooledConnectionLifetime (available since .NET Core 2.1) recycles pooled connections so new ones resolve DNS again, which a singleton client otherwise never does.
- web-api-12 | web-api | middle | multi | Asks the reader to select the transports ASP.NET Core SignalR can negotiate, from a list including gRPC streaming and raw TCP. | ASP.NET Core SignalR supports WebSockets, Server-Sent Events and Long Polling and falls back between them in that order.
- web-api-13 | web-api | senior | find-bug | A non-runnable hub class keeps a per-user counter in an instance field and the reader must find the line that loses the state between calls. | Hub instances are transient and created for each hub method invocation, so state stored in hub fields does not survive and must live in a separate service or store.
- web-api-14 | web-api | senior | open | Asks how gRPC deadlines differ from a plain client timeout and how they should flow through a chain of service calls. | A deadline is sent to the server, which can observe it through the call cancellation token, and propagating it to downstream calls stops the whole chain from working past the moment the original caller gave up.
- web-api-15 | web-api | senior | situation | After scaling a SignalR app from one to three instances behind a load balancer, some clients fail to connect and broadcasts reach only part of the users; the reader plans the diagnosis and fix. | Each server only knows its own connections, so scale-out needs sticky sessions for negotiation and fallback transports plus a backplane such as Redis or Azure SignalR Service to fan out messages.
- web-api-16 | web-api | senior | open | Asks how an HTTP API should expose an operation that takes minutes, without holding the request open. | The API returns 202 Accepted with a Location to a status resource that the client polls, and that resource reports progress and finally points to the result.
- web-api-17 | web-api | lead | situation | A public API used by external partners needs a breaking change to a response contract; the reader decides how the team ships it without breaking clients. | Ship the change as a new version alongside the old one, announce a deprecation window with Deprecation and Sunset signals and usage monitoring, and retire the old version only when traffic and agreed dates allow.
- web-api-18 | web-api | architect | situation | A platform with a public partner API and dozens of internal services must choose a request-response protocol for each side; the reader weighs REST and gRPC across years of evolution. | REST with JSON suits the public edge for reach, browser and tooling support, while gRPC suits internal calls for strict contracts, streaming and efficiency, at the cost of HTTP/2 requirements and weaker browser and proxy support.
- security-01 | security | junior | open | Ask the candidate to explain the difference between authentication and authorization and give an ASP.NET Core example of each step in a request. | Authentication establishes who the caller is (it builds the ClaimsPrincipal from a cookie or token), while authorization decides whether that known identity may perform this action, and it always runs after authentication.
- security-02 | security | junior | single | Ask who can read the claims inside a signed JWT (JWS) that the API issues to a browser client. | A signed JWT is only base64url-encoded and signed, not encrypted, so anyone holding the token can decode and read its payload; the signature only prevents tampering.
- security-03 | security | junior | multi | Ask the candidate to pick every acceptable way to store user passwords from a list that mixes PBKDF2 with a per-user salt, the ASP.NET Core Identity PasswordHasher, unsalted SHA-256 and reversible AES encryption. | Passwords must be stored with a deliberately slow, salted one-way key-derivation function such as PBKDF2 (as Identity's PasswordHasher does), never with a fast unsalted hash or reversible encryption.
- security-04 | security | junior | single | Ask where the Secret Manager tool (dotnet user-secrets) stores values and whether it is suitable for production secrets. | User secrets are stored as plain, unencrypted JSON in the developer's user profile outside the project tree, so they only keep secrets out of source control during development and are not a production secret store.
- security-05 | security | middle | open | Ask what a CORS policy actually protects against and why it does not stop a script or curl from calling the API. | CORS is enforced by the browser and only relaxes the same-origin policy for reading cross-origin responses, so it is not server-side access control and non-browser clients ignore it entirely.
- security-06 | security | middle | find-bug | Show an ASP.NET Core CORS policy that combines SetIsOriginAllowed(_ => true) with AllowCredentials for a cookie-authenticated API and ask for the line that creates the vulnerability (not runnable, ASP.NET Core code). | Allowing every origin while also allowing credentials reflects any Origin into Access-Control-Allow-Origin with credentials, so any website can read authenticated responses on behalf of a logged-in user.
- security-07 | security | middle | multi | Ask which of several endpoint setups (cookie-authenticated form posts, cookie-authenticated JSON API, API authenticated only by a bearer token in the Authorization header, anonymous read-only GET) need antiforgery protection. | CSRF works because the browser attaches cookies automatically to cross-site requests, so state-changing endpoints authenticated by cookies need antiforgery tokens while endpoints that require a manually attached Authorization header do not.
- security-08 | security | middle | single | Ask which request can still carry a SameSite=Lax authentication cookie from another site and therefore remains exposed to CSRF. | SameSite=Lax withholds the cookie on cross-site subrequests and POSTs but still sends it on top-level GET navigations, so an endpoint that changes state on GET stays vulnerable.
- security-09 | security | middle | open | Ask which OAuth 2.0 flow a SPA or mobile app should use and what attack PKCE prevents. | Public clients should use the authorization code flow with PKCE, because the code_verifier proves that whoever redeems the authorization code is the client that started the flow, so an intercepted code is useless, and the implicit flow is no longer recommended.
- security-10 | security | middle | open | Ask how OpenID Connect differs from OAuth 2.0 and why an API must not accept an ID token as a bearer credential. | OAuth 2.0 is delegated authorization that issues access tokens for resource servers, while OIDC adds authentication by issuing an ID token whose audience is the client application, so APIs must accept only access tokens issued for them.
- security-11 | security | middle | multi | Ask which TokenValidationParameters settings weaken JWT bearer validation, from a list mixing ValidateAudience = false, ValidateLifetime = false, RequireSignedTokens = false, a small ClockSkew and a configured ValidIssuer. | Turning off audience, lifetime or signature requirements lets tokens for other APIs, expired tokens or unsigned tokens through, while a small clock skew and an explicit valid issuer tighten validation.
- security-12 | security | senior | open | Ask how to log out a user or revoke access immediately when the API uses stateless JWT access tokens, and what each option costs. | A self-contained JWT stays valid until it expires, so revocation relies on short access-token lifetimes plus revocable, rotated refresh tokens, or on a server-side check (denylist by jti or introspection) that gives up statelessness.
- security-13 | security | senior | find-bug | Show a runnable BCL snippet (.NET 10 on Linux) that builds a download path with Path.Combine(baseDir, userFileName) and prints the resulting path for a user-supplied name, then ask for the line that lets the caller escape the upload directory. | Path.Combine returns the second argument unchanged when it is rooted and does not normalise '..' segments, so the code must resolve the path with Path.GetFullPath and verify that it still starts with the base directory.
- security-14 | security | senior | single | Ask how an attacker can forge a token for an API that signs with RS256 when the validator trusts the alg header of the incoming token. | If the validator lets the token choose HS256, the attacker signs with HMAC using the publicly known RSA public key as the secret, so the validator must pin the allowed algorithms and key types instead of trusting the header.
- security-15 | security | senior | situation | A production database connection string with a password was committed to a shared Git repository three weeks ago; ask what the candidate does and in what order. | The secret must be treated as compromised and rotated first, because rewriting Git history cannot recall existing clones, followed by checking access logs, moving the secret to a managed store such as Key Vault and adding secret scanning to prevent recurrence.
- security-16 | security | senior | open | Ask why [Authorize(Roles = "Customer")] on GET /orders/{id} still lets one customer read another customer's order and how to fix it in ASP.NET Core. | Role or policy checks on the endpoint do not look at the specific resource, so the handler must load the order and run a resource-based check (IAuthorizationService.AuthorizeAsync with the order) that it belongs to the caller.
- security-17 | security | lead | situation | NuGet audit reports a critical vulnerability in a transitive package two days before a release, and the team wants to ship anyway; ask how the lead decides and what process changes follow. | The lead assesses whether the vulnerable code path is reachable and exploitable, fixes it by referencing a patched version directly or upgrading the parent package, records any accepted risk explicitly, and makes NuGet auditing a CI gate so the issue is found continuously rather than before a release.
- security-18 | security | architect | situation | A platform of twenty services currently validates user tokens only at the API gateway and passes a plain user-id header internally; ask how the candidate would redesign authentication and authorization between services. | Internal services should not trust a forgeable header behind the gateway: each service validates an access token scoped to its own audience, user context is passed downstream through token exchange or on-behalf-of flows, and machine-only calls use client credentials.
- ef-core-01 | ef-core | junior | single | After calling context.Add(entity) and before SaveChanges, which EntityState does the change tracker report for the entity? | Add marks the entity as Added, so SaveChanges will issue an INSERT for it; nothing is sent to the database before SaveChanges.
- ef-core-02 | ef-core | junior | open | What does AsNoTracking change in a query, and when should a developer use it? | AsNoTracking returns entities that the context does not track, so it skips snapshotting and identity bookkeeping and suits read-only data; changes to those entities are not saved by SaveChanges.
- ef-core-03 | ef-core | junior | single | What does `dotnet ef migrations add` do compared with `dotnet ef database update`? | `migrations add` only compares the model with the model snapshot and generates migration code files; the schema changes reach the database only when the migration is applied, for example with `database update`.
- ef-core-04 | ef-core | junior | multi | Which of the listed approaches load an order's Items collection in EF Core (Include, Entry(order).Collection(o => o.Items).Load(), lazy loading proxies when configured, and DbSet.Find on the order alone)? | Eager loading with Include, explicit loading with Entry().Collection().Load() and configured lazy loading all load the collection, while Find loads only the order itself.
- ef-core-05 | ef-core | junior | open | If one SaveChanges call inserts an order and updates stock and the update fails, what happens to the insert, and why? | By default a single SaveChanges call runs all its commands in one database transaction, so a failure rolls back every change of that call.
- ef-core-06 | ef-core | middle | find-bug | Find the line where a search query passes an interpolated user string to FromSqlRaw, and explain the fix. | FromSqlRaw with an interpolated string concatenates user input into SQL and enables SQL injection; FromSql or FromSqlInterpolated (EF Core 7 and later for FromSql) turn interpolated values into DbParameters.
- ef-core-07 | ef-core | middle | find-bug | Find the line in a report loop over orders that, with lazy loading proxies enabled, issues one extra query per order by reading order.Customer.Name. | Touching an unloaded navigation property inside the loop triggers a lazy load per iteration, which is the N+1 pattern; loading Customer up front with Include or a projection removes it.
- ef-core-08 | ef-core | middle | find-bug | Find the lines of a scaffolded migration, created after renaming the Name property to FullName, that would lose existing data. | The scaffolder can produce DropColumn plus AddColumn for a rename, which deletes the data; the migration must be edited to use RenameColumn instead.
- ef-core-09 | ef-core | middle | single | An entity has a rowversion concurrency token and another user changed the row after it was loaded; what does SaveChanges do? | EF Core adds the original token to the UPDATE's WHERE clause, sees zero affected rows and throws DbUpdateConcurrencyException instead of overwriting the row.
- ef-core-10 | ef-core | middle | multi | Which statements about ExecuteUpdate and ExecuteDelete in EF Core 7 and later are true? | They run a single SQL statement immediately without loading entities or calling SaveChanges, and they do not update entities already tracked by the context, which can then hold stale values.
- ef-core-11 | ef-core | middle | multi | Which ways of applying migrations does the EF Core documentation recommend for production deployments? | Generated SQL scripts (including idempotent scripts) and migration bundles (EF Core 6 and later) are recommended, while calling Database.Migrate at application startup is discouraged for production.
- ef-core-12 | ef-core | middle | open | When do you need Database.BeginTransaction in EF Core, and how do you use it correctly with several SaveChanges calls? | An explicit transaction is needed only when several SaveChanges calls or mixed raw SQL must commit or roll back together; you begin it, call SaveChanges as needed and Commit, and disposing without Commit rolls back.
- ef-core-13 | ef-core | middle | single | Two tracking queries on the same DbContext return the customer with Id 5; how do the two results relate? | A tracking query resolves identities through the change tracker, so both queries return the same instance and the second does not overwrite its tracked values with database values.
- ef-core-14 | ef-core | senior | situation | A nightly import uses one DbContext to process two million rows; memory grows steadily and each SaveChanges gets slower. What do you do? | Every tracked entity stays in the change tracker and DetectChanges scans all of them, so the fix is to process in batches with a short-lived context per batch (or ChangeTracker.Clear) and avoid tracking for read-only data.
- ef-core-15 | ef-core | senior | open | How does EF Core detect changes to plain entities by default, what does it cost, and when is turning off AutoDetectChangesEnabled justified? | Snapshot change tracking compares every tracked entity with its original snapshot on DetectChanges, which runs automatically from several APIs, so the cost grows with the number of tracked entities; disabling auto-detection helps hot loops only if DetectChanges is then called explicitly.
- ef-core-16 | ef-core | senior | single | With EnableRetryOnFailure configured, what happens when code calls BeginTransaction directly, and what is the correct pattern? | A retrying execution strategy rejects user-initiated transactions with an InvalidOperationException, so the whole transactional block must be wrapped in Database.CreateExecutionStrategy().Execute so it can be retried as a unit.
- ef-core-17 | ef-core | senior | open | A query includes two collection navigations; compare a single query with AsSplitQuery and explain when each is the better choice. | A single query with several collection Includes multiplies rows (cartesian explosion), while a split query avoids it at the cost of extra round trips and no consistency guarantee between the separate queries if data changes concurrently.
- ef-core-18 | ef-core | senior | situation | Support reports that edits to customer records are silently lost when two operators save the same record; how do you detect and resolve these conflicts? | Add a concurrency token so the second save raises DbUpdateConcurrencyException, then resolve it deliberately using the entry's current, original and database values (GetDatabaseValues) to retry, merge or ask the user, instead of last-writer-wins.
- ef-core-19 | ef-core | lead | situation | Your team must rename a column used by a service deployed with rolling updates; how do you plan the migrations and releases so nothing breaks? | During a rolling deploy old and new application versions run against the same schema, so the change must be split into backward-compatible steps across releases (add the new column, copy and dual-write, switch reads, drop the old column later).
- ef-core-20 | ef-core | architect | open | In a large, long-lived system, where would you use EF Core LINQ and change tracking and where raw SQL, and what rules keep the raw SQL safe and maintainable? | Use EF Core for writes and aggregate consistency and allow raw SQL (FromSql, SqlQuery in EF Core 8 and later, or a micro-ORM) for read paths LINQ cannot express efficiently, always parameterized and kept in a known place with tests, accepting that raw SQL is invisible to migrations and model refactoring.
- databases-01 | databases | junior | open | Explain the difference between a clustered and a nonclustered index and why a table can have only one clustered index. | The leaf level of a clustered index is the table data itself, sorted by the key, so there can be only one; a nonclustered index is a separate structure whose leaf rows point back to the data through the clustering key or a row locator.
- databases-02 | databases | junior | single | Which standard isolation level allows a transaction to read rows changed by another transaction that has not committed yet? | Only READ UNCOMMITTED permits dirty reads; READ COMMITTED and every stricter level read only committed data.
- databases-03 | databases | junior | open | What is normalization up to third normal form and which problem does it solve in a table that stores a customer's city next to every order? | Normalization removes redundant data and transitive dependencies on non-key columns, so each fact is stored once and update, insert and delete anomalies disappear.
- databases-04 | databases | junior | multi | Select every real cost of adding a nonclustered index to a table. | Each index must be maintained on every INSERT, DELETE and on UPDATE of its columns and takes extra storage, while it does not slow down reads that do not use it.
- databases-05 | databases | junior | single | A transaction holds a shared lock on a row; which request from another transaction on the same row is granted immediately? | Shared locks are compatible with other shared locks, while an exclusive lock is incompatible with both shared and exclusive locks and must wait.
- databases-06 | databases | middle | find-bug | Find the line in a T-SQL query that forces a full index scan although an index on CreatedAt exists (WHERE YEAR(CreatedAt) = 2024). | Wrapping the indexed column in a function makes the predicate non-sargable, so the optimizer cannot seek; rewriting it as a range CreatedAt >= '2024-01-01' AND CreatedAt < '2025-01-01' allows an index seek.
- databases-07 | databases | middle | single | Given an index on (CustomerId, CreatedAt), which of several WHERE clauses can be answered with an index seek on both columns? | A composite index is sorted by its leading column first, so a seek needs an equality or range on CustomerId; a filter on CreatedAt alone cannot seek.
- databases-08 | databases | middle | open | What does a Key Lookup operator in an execution plan mean, when does it become expensive and how do INCLUDE columns remove it? | A key lookup fetches columns missing from the nonclustered index row by row from the clustered index; adding those columns as INCLUDE makes the index covering so the query is answered from the index alone.
- databases-09 | databases | middle | multi | Select every read anomaly that can still occur under the READ COMMITTED isolation level. | READ COMMITTED prevents dirty reads only, so non-repeatable reads and phantom reads remain possible, while dirty writes are prevented at every level.
- databases-10 | databases | middle | find-bug | Find the line in a T-SQL procedure that reads a balance with SELECT, computes the new value in a variable and writes it back with UPDATE SET Balance = @newBalance, losing concurrent withdrawals. | Under READ COMMITTED the shared lock of the SELECT is released before the UPDATE, so two sessions read the same value and the later absolute UPDATE overwrites the earlier one; an atomic UPDATE SET Balance = Balance - @amount WHERE Balance >= @amount fixes it.
- databases-11 | databases | middle | open | When is it reasonable to denormalize a relational schema, and what do you have to accept and put in place when you do? | Denormalize only for a measured read bottleneck such as heavy joins or aggregates, accepting duplicated data and update anomalies, and keep one source of truth with a defined way to keep the copies in sync.
- databases-12 | databases | middle | single | In SQL Server with READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON, what happens when a READ COMMITTED query reads a row that another transaction has updated but not committed? | The reader gets the last committed version of the row from the version store without waiting for the writer's exclusive lock.
- databases-13 | databases | senior | situation | Under load two stored procedures that update Orders and Inventory regularly fail with deadlock error 1205; how do you diagnose and fix it? | Capture the deadlock graph from the system_health Extended Events session, find the resources taken in opposite order, then make both paths access tables in the same order, shorten transactions, add indexes that avoid scans and retry the victim.
- databases-14 | databases | senior | situation | A parameterized query is fast for most customers but takes minutes for one large customer, and the slowness comes and goes after restarts; what is happening and what do you do? | The cached plan was compiled for the parameter values of the first call (parameter sniffing) and is wrong for skewed data; confirm with Query Store and fix with plan forcing, OPTIMIZE FOR, RECOMPILE or a query change after measuring.
- databases-15 | databases | senior | open | An actual execution plan shows an operator estimated at 10 rows that returned 2 million; what does this indicate and what consequences does it have for the plan? | A large estimate error points to stale or missing statistics or a predicate the cardinality estimator cannot model, which leads to wrong join types, wrong access methods and undersized memory grants that spill to tempdb.
- databases-16 | databases | senior | multi | Select every true statement about lock escalation in SQL Server. | SQL Server escalates many row or page locks taken by one statement on one object (around 5000) directly to a table or partition lock to save lock memory, which can block concurrent sessions; it never escalates rows to pages.
- databases-17 | databases | lead | situation | A core table has gathered dozens of indexes added ticket by ticket, write latency keeps growing and every team wants one more index; how do you decide what to change and what process to set up? | Measure index usage and write cost from usage statistics and Query Store, remove or merge unused and overlapping indexes in staged, reversible steps, and require a review with a plan and workload evidence before any new index instead of accepting missing-index suggestions blindly.
- databases-18 | databases | architect | open | How do you decide between a relational database and a document store for a new service's main data, and which decisions are hard to reverse later? | The choice follows the access patterns: a document store gains horizontal partitioning and aggregate-shaped reads by giving up ad-hoc joins and cheap multi-entity transactions, and its partition key and document shape are long-lived decisions that are costly to change.
- testing-01 | testing | junior | single | Asks which of several test descriptions is a unit test rather than an integration or end-to-end test. | A unit test exercises a small piece of behaviour in isolation from out-of-process dependencies such as databases, file systems and networks, so it is fast and deterministic.
- testing-02 | testing | junior | open | Asks the candidate to explain the Arrange-Act-Assert structure of a test and why each test should have a single Act step. | Separating setup, the one action under test and the checks makes a test readable and ensures that a failure points to one behaviour.
- testing-03 | testing | junior | single | Asks what an xUnit [Theory] with three [InlineData] attributes does compared with a [Fact]. | A [Theory] is a parameterized test that runs once per data row, so three [InlineData] rows give three separately reported test cases, while a [Fact] takes no parameters and runs once.
- testing-04 | testing | junior | open | Asks the candidate to describe the red-green-refactor cycle of test-driven development and the purpose of each step. | Write a failing test first to prove it can fail, write the minimal code to make it pass, then refactor with the passing tests as a safety net.
- testing-05 | testing | junior | single | Asks which signature a test method that awaits an async method under test should have. | The test must be declared async Task so the test framework can await completion and observe exceptions; an async void test returns nothing the framework can wait on.
- testing-06 | testing | middle | open | Asks how a mock differs from a fake and when each is the better choice for a dependency. | A fake is a working lightweight implementation checked through resulting state, while a mock records and verifies interactions, so mocks fit outgoing calls whose occurrence is the behaviour and fakes fit dependencies whose state the test reads back.
- testing-07 | testing | middle | find-bug | A hand-written console test calls an async method that should throw ArgumentException inside try/catch without awaiting it and prints FAIL; find the line. | An async method stores its exception in the returned Task instead of throwing synchronously, so the call must be awaited inside the try block for the exception to surface.
- testing-08 | testing | middle | find-bug | Two hand-written test methods run in sequence against a fake repository that keeps items in a static list, so the second test sees one extra item and prints FAIL; find the line. | Static state in a test double survives between tests and makes results depend on execution order, so each test needs its own fresh instance.
- testing-09 | testing | middle | single | Asks which statement correctly describes what WebApplicationFactory<TEntryPoint> does in an ASP.NET Core integration test. | It starts the application's real entry point on an in-memory TestServer, so requests from its HttpClient pass through the full middleware pipeline without opening a network port, and services can be replaced with ConfigureTestServices.
- testing-10 | testing | middle | multi | Asks which differences make the EF Core in-memory provider an unreliable substitute for a relational database in tests. | The in-memory provider is not a relational database: it does not enforce relational constraints, has no real transactions, cannot run raw SQL and can accept queries the real provider would fail to translate.
- testing-11 | testing | middle | multi | Asks which statements about using TimeProvider (introduced in .NET 8) to test time-dependent and delay-based code are true. | Injecting TimeProvider instead of reading DateTime.UtcNow or calling Task.Delay directly lets a test substitute FakeTimeProvider from Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing and advance time explicitly without real waiting.
- testing-12 | testing | senior | situation | About 5 percent of CI runs fail on different tests that always pass locally; what does the candidate do and in what order? | Retrying hides the defect; the fix is to quarantine the flaky tests and find the nondeterministic source, such as wall-clock time, test order, parallel test collections sharing an external resource, or unawaited async work.
- testing-13 | testing | senior | open | Asks how to keep integration tests that run against a real database engine in a container isolated from each other and still fast. | Create the schema once per run and then isolate each test by rolling back a per-test transaction or resetting data to a known state, rather than recreating the database for every test.
- testing-14 | testing | senior | multi | Asks which testing practices make a suite break on refactorings that do not change observable behaviour. | Tests that verify calls to internal collaborators, verify query calls on stubs or test private methods through reflection couple to implementation details, while asserting on outputs and outgoing side effects survives refactoring.
- testing-15 | testing | lead | situation | After the team introduced an 80 percent line-coverage gate in CI, reviews find tests that call code without meaningful assertions; what does the candidate do as tech lead? | Coverage shows which code is untested, not that it is tested well, so a hard target invites gaming; treat coverage as a diagnostic, review test quality in code review and consider mutation testing on critical code instead of raising the number.
- testing-16 | testing | architect | open | Asks how to verify compatibility between many independently deployed services without depending on one shared end-to-end environment. | Consumer-driven contract tests let each provider check, in its own pipeline, that it still satisfies its consumers' expectations, so only a thin layer of end-to-end tests over critical user journeys remains.
- patterns-01 | patterns | junior | output | What does a snippet print when the same List<int>.Sort call is given two different IComparer<int> strategies in turn? | The comparer object is the strategy: Sort runs the same algorithm, and only the comparison passed in decides the order, so swapping the comparer reverses the output.
- patterns-02 | patterns | junior | output | What does a snippet print when a text formatter is wrapped first in a bracket decorator and then in an upper-case decorator, each adding its effect around the inner call? | The outermost decorator runs last on the result, so the order of wrapping decides the final text.
- patterns-03 | patterns | junior | single | Which GoF pattern do the BCL interfaces IObservable<T> and IObserver<T> implement? | IObservable<T> is the subject that pushes OnNext, OnError and OnCompleted notifications to subscribed IObserver<T> instances, which is the Observer pattern.
- patterns-04 | patterns | junior | multi | Which of these System.IO types are decorators that wrap another Stream and add behaviour to it: BufferedStream, GZipStream, CryptoStream, MemoryStream, FileStream? | BufferedStream, GZipStream and CryptoStream take an inner Stream in their constructor and add buffering, compression or encryption, while MemoryStream and FileStream are backing stores with no inner stream.
- patterns-05 | patterns | junior | open | What problem does the Adapter pattern solve, and how would you use it to plug a third-party SMS client into your own INotificationSender interface? | An adapter implements the interface your code expects and translates calls to an existing incompatible API, so the client code never depends on the third-party type directly.
- patterns-06 | patterns | middle | output | What does a snippet print when a request passes through a chain of three discount handlers where each handler either handles the request and stops or forwards it to the next one? | The first handler in the chain whose condition matches handles the request and does not call its successor, so later matching handlers never run.
- patterns-07 | patterns | middle | output | What does a snippet print after a prototype is cloned with MemberwiseClone and the clone adds an item to its List<string> field and changes its int field? | MemberwiseClone makes a shallow copy: the int field is copied by value, but the list field still references the same List object, so the original sees the added item.
- patterns-08 | patterns | middle | output | What does a snippet print when a base class constructor calls an abstract template-method step that the derived class implements using a field assigned in the derived constructor body? | The base constructor runs before the derived constructor body, so the overridden step sees the field at its default value.
- patterns-09 | patterns | middle | find-bug | Find the line that makes a Singleton create a new instance on every access, so a counter stored in it never grows past 1. | The property is declared as `public static Counter Instance => new Counter();`, an expression-bodied getter that runs `new` on every read, instead of `{ get; } = new Counter();` which initializes once.
- patterns-10 | patterns | middle | single | What is the main reason resolving dependencies from an injected IServiceProvider inside class methods is considered an anti-pattern? | The class hides its real dependencies behind a generic locator, so its constructor no longer states what it needs and missing registrations fail only at run time when the method executes.
- patterns-11 | patterns | middle | multi | Which pairs correctly match a C# language feature with the GoF pattern it makes a hand-written class hierarchy unnecessary for: event and Observer, Func<T> delegate and Strategy, yield return and Iterator, lock statement and Singleton, using statement and Decorator? | Events implement Observer, delegates replace one-method Strategy classes and yield return generates an Iterator, while lock and using are synchronization and disposal constructs unrelated to Singleton or Decorator.
- patterns-12 | patterns | senior | output | What does a snippet print when a Lazy<T> singleton whose factory increments a counter and throws is read twice inside try/catch blocks and the counter is then printed? | Lazy<T> created with a factory in the default ExecutionAndPublication mode caches the exception, so the second read rethrows it without running the factory again and the counter stays at 1.
- patterns-13 | patterns | senior | single | Why is a hand-written double-checked locking Singleton unnecessary in C# when a static readonly field initializer is used? | The runtime guarantees that a type's static initialization runs exactly once and is thread-safe, so a static readonly field already gives a correctly published single instance without explicit locking.
- patterns-14 | patterns | senior | open | When does a classic Visitor (as in ExpressionVisitor) still pay off in C# compared with a switch expression with type patterns over a closed hierarchy? | Visitor makes adding operations cheap and lets the compiler force every node type to be handled through abstract Visit methods and reusable traversal, while a switch expression is simpler when the hierarchy is small and stable but gives no exhaustiveness for open class hierarchies and spreads traversal logic.
- patterns-15 | patterns | lead | situation | A pull request adds an abstract factory, a strategy interface and a builder around a report export that has exactly one format and no planned second one; as the tech lead, what do you do? | Patterns are justified by a variation that exists now, so the lead asks for the concrete need, agrees a simpler design that can be refactored when a second format appears, and turns the case into a team guideline rather than a personal veto.
- patterns-16 | patterns | architect | open | Across dozens of services maintained for years, what are the trade-offs of implementing logging, caching and retries as Decorators around every interface versus a shared pipeline such as DelegatingHandler chains or middleware? | Per-interface decorators give precise, testable control but multiply boilerplate, hide execution order in DI registration and drift between services, while a shared pipeline centralizes policy and order at the cost of coarser granularity, so the choice depends on how uniform the concern is.
- architecture-01 | architecture | junior | single | In a classic three-layer application (presentation, business logic, data access), which layer should hold a rule such as 'orders over 1000 get a 5% discount'? | Business rules belong in the business logic (domain) layer, not in UI handlers or SQL, so that every entry point applies them and they can be tested without the UI or the database.
- architecture-02 | architecture | middle | single | In a clean architecture solution with Core, Infrastructure and Web projects, which project reference arrangement is correct for a repository used by the application core? | Dependencies point inward: Core defines the repository interface and references neither Infrastructure nor Web, while Infrastructure references Core and implements the interface.
- architecture-03 | architecture | middle | multi | From a list of components (HTTP controller, message consumer, CLI command, SQL repository, SMTP email sender, payment gateway client), select all driven (secondary) adapters. | Driven adapters are called by the application through ports it owns (persistence, email, external services), whereas driving adapters such as controllers, consumers and CLI commands call into the application.
- architecture-04 | architecture | middle | find-bug | A runnable snippet models Money as a plain class and compares two equal amounts, printing that the prices differ; find the line that breaks value-object semantics. | A value object is defined by its values and must have structural equality; a plain class compares by reference, so the fix is a record (C# 9 and later) or overridden Equals and GetHashCode.
- architecture-05 | architecture | middle | open | When does splitting commands and queries into separate models pay off, and when is it unnecessary complexity for a service? | CQRS pays off when read and write needs diverge (different shapes, complex domain logic on writes, very different load); for simple CRUD over one model it adds code and indirection with no benefit.
- architecture-06 | architecture | senior | find-bug | A runnable Order aggregate enforces a maximum of three lines in AddLine but exposes its lines as a public List, and the caller ends up with four lines; find the defective line. | Exposing the mutable collection lets callers bypass the aggregate root and break its invariant; the collection must be a private field exposed as IReadOnlyCollection so all changes go through the root.
- architecture-07 | architecture | senior | open | Why is it recommended to modify only one aggregate per transaction and to reference other aggregates by identity, and how are rules that span aggregates handled? | An aggregate is the consistency boundary: its invariants are enforced atomically within it, while rules spanning aggregates are kept eventually consistent, which keeps transactions small and avoids contention and large object graphs.
- architecture-08 | architecture | senior | multi | Select all statements about CQRS that are true: it requires event sourcing, it requires a separate read database, it separates the model used for updates from the model used for reads, a separate read store makes reads eventually consistent with writes. | CQRS only mandates separate read and write models; event sourcing and a separate read store are optional, and only when a separate store is used do reads become eventually consistent.
